questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $n$ is a positive integer, then $2.4^{2 n+1}+3^{3 n+1}$ is divisible by:
questions.solution:
Let $P(n)=2 \cdot 4^{2 n+1}+3^{3 n+1}$
Then $P(1)=2.4^3+3^4=209$, which is divisible by 11 but not divisible by 2,7 or 27 .
Further, let $P(k)=2.4^{2 k+1}+3^{3 k+1}$ is divisible by 11 , that is,
$2.4^{2 k+1}+3^{3 k+1}=11 q$ for some integer q. Now
$\begin{aligned} \\ \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{k}+1) & =2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+3}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+4} \\ \\ & =2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1} \cdot 4^2+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \cdot 3^3 \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+27 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+(16+11) \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16\left[2 \cdot 4^{2 \mathrm{k}+1}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1}\right]+11 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =16 \cdot 11 \mathrm{q}+11 \cdot 3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1} \\ \\ & =11\left(16 \mathrm{q}+3^{3 \mathrm{k}+1}\right)=11 \mathrm{~m} \\ \end{aligned}$
where $m=16 q+3^{3 k+1}$ is another integer.
$\therefore \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{k}+1)$ is divisible by 11 .

questions.solution:
Here, $\mathrm{y}^{\mathrm{x}}=\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{y}-\mathrm{x}}$
Taking log on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \log y^x=\log e^{y-x} \\ \\ & \quad\left(\because \log a^b=b \log a \text { and } \log e=1\right) \\ \end{aligned}$
$\Rightarrow x \log y=(y-x) \log e \Rightarrow x \log y=y-x \ldots(i)$
On differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get

$\begin{aligned} \\ & =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[(2-h)^2-1\right]=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[4+h^2-4 h-1\right] \\ \\ & =\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}\left[h^2-4 h+3\right]=0-0+3=3 \\ \end{aligned}$
and $\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}} f(x)=\lim _{x \rightarrow 2^{+}}(2 x+3)$
$=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}[2(2+h)+3]=\lim _{h \rightarrow 0}[4+2 h+3]=7$
Hence the quadratic equation whose roots are 3 and 7 is given by $x^2-(3+7) x+(3+7)=0 \Rightarrow x^2-10 x+21=0$

$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{T}}=\frac{2}{9 \eta}(\rho-\sigma) \mathrm{r}^2 \mathrm{~g} \\ \\ & \therefore \mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{T}} \propto \mathrm{r}^2 \\ \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{v}_1}{\mathrm{v}_2}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{R}}\right)^2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{10}{\mathrm{v}_2}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2\left(\because \mathrm{v}_1=10 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s} \text { given }\right) \\ \\ & \quad \Rightarrow \mathrm{v}_2=40 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s} \\ \end{aligned}$

[Assume length of wires A and B are same]

Elongation produced in the wire is given b

questions.q: A thin prism $P_1$ with an angle $6^{\circ}$ and made of glass of refractive index 1.54 is combined with another prism $\mathrm{P}_2$ made from glass of refractive index 1.72 to produce dispersion without average deviation. The angle of prism $\mathrm{P}_2$ is :
questions.solution:
Angle of deviation for first prism
$\delta_1=A_1\left(\mu_1-1\right)=6(1.54-1)$
Angle of deviation for second prism
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \delta_2=A_2\left(\mu_2-1\right) \\ \\ & =A_2(1.72-1) \\ \end{aligned}$
For dispersion without deviation
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \delta_1=\delta_2 \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 6^{\circ}(1.54-1)=\mathrm{A}_2(1.72-1) \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{A}_2=\frac{6^{\circ} \times 0.54}{0.72}=\frac{18^{\circ}}{4}=4.5^{\circ} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A bowl filled with very hot soup cools from $98^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $86^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ in 2 minutes when the room temperature is $22^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. How long it will take to cool from $75^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $69^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ?
questions.solution:
The rate of heat flow is given by
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}=-K\left(T-T_0\right) \Rightarrow \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}=-K\left(T_{a v g}-T_0\right) \\ \\ & \text { Initially } T_{a v g}=\frac{T_1+T_2}{2} \\ \\ & \text { Here, } T_1=98^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \\ & T_2=86^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & \text { (i) } \frac{\mathrm{ms} \times 12}{2}=-\mathrm{K}\left(\frac{98+86}{2}-22\right) \\ & 6=-\frac{\mathrm{K}}{\mathrm{ms}}\left[\frac{98+86}{2}-22\right] \quad(\because \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\mathrm{ms} \Delta \mathrm{T})\end{aligned}$


Now, cool from $\mathrm{T}_1^{\prime}=75^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{T}_2=69^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \\ & \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_1^{\prime}+\mathrm{T}_2^{\prime}}{2}=\frac{75+69}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$
(ii) $\frac{\mathrm{ms} \times 6}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=-\mathrm{K}\left(\frac{75+69}{2}-22\right)$

Divide equation (ii) by (i), we have
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \frac{6}{\Delta t(6)}=\frac{50}{70} \\ \\ & \Delta t=\frac{7}{5}=1.4 \mathrm{~min} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: A hypothetical gas expands adiabatically such that its volume changes from 08 litres to 27 litres. If the ratio of final pressure of the gas to initial pressure of the gas is $\frac{16}{81}$. Then the ratio of $\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}}$ will be.
questions.solution:
In adiabatic process
$\begin{aligned} \\ & \mathrm{PV}^\gamma=\text { constant } \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1^\gamma=\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2^\gamma \\ \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\mathrm{P}_1}{\mathrm{P}_2}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{\mathrm{~V}_1}\right)^\gamma \Rightarrow \frac{81}{16}=\left(\frac{27}{8}\right)^\gamma \\ \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^2=\left(\frac{9 \times 3}{4 \times 2}\right)^\gamma \Rightarrow\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{2-\gamma}=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^\gamma \\ \\ & \Rightarrow\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{2-\gamma}=\left(\frac{9}{4}\right)^{\gamma / 2} \Rightarrow 2-\gamma=\frac{\gamma}{2} \\ \\ & \Rightarrow 2=\frac{3}{2} \gamma \Rightarrow \gamma=\frac{4}{3} \\ \end{aligned}$

questions.q: On a temperature scale ' $X$ '. The boiling point of water is $65^{\circ} \mathrm{X}$ and the freezing point is $-15^{\circ} \mathrm{X}$. Assume that the $\mathrm{X}$ scale is linear. The equivalent temperature corresponding to $-95^{\circ} \mathrm{X}$ on the Farenheit scale would be:
questions.solution:
Boiling point of water, $=$ UFP $65^{\circ}$
Freezing point of water, $=\mathrm{LFP}-15^{\circ}$
$\frac{\mathrm{X}-\mathrm{LFP}}{\mathrm{UFP}-\mathrm{LFP}}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{F}}-32}{212-32}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-95-(-15)}{65-(-15)}=\frac{\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{F}}-32}{180}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-80}{80}=\frac{T_F-32}{180} \Rightarrow T_F=-180+32$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{F}}=-148^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$

$v=r^a \rho^b s^c$. The values of $a, b$ and $c$ respectively are
